name: Does Colorado’s dry climate affect kitchen molding installations in Denver?

mainEntity.name: Does Colorado’s dry climate affect kitchen molding installations in Denver?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Denver and surrounding areas, the semi-arid climate and low indoor humidity cause wood materials to contract, which can open up molding joints if proper techniques are omitted. Sudden humidity shifts between dry winters and summer storms cause standard miter cuts to pull apart at corners. Finish contractors working across Denver homes use coped joints rather than simple 45-degree miter cuts on inside corners, along with flexible adhesives and expansion-tolerant caulking, ensuring trim stays tight and crack-free despite Colorado’s extreme indoor moisture swings.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, Denver’s dry air causes wood to shrink. Contractors use coped inside joints and flexible caulk rather than basic miters to prevent seams from separating.
